compliance.seismic: Designed to comply with Zone 4 earthquake requirements per GR-63, Issue 4

environmental.altitude: AFO builds no performance degradation to 1828.8 m (6000 ft); AFI builds none at sea level
environmental.humidity: 5 to 90 percent noncondensing (up to 93 percent short term)
environmental.storage-temp: -40 to 70 C (-40 to 158 F) in the shipping container

features.channelization: ports 0 to 31 take 4 x 10, 4 x 25 and 2 x 50 GbE breakouts. Ports 32 to 63 take 2 x 50 GbE before Junos OS 19.1R1. From 19.1R1 on, any port
features.optics-qsfp28: 100 GbE QSFP28 and 40 GbE QSFP+ transceivers. DAC and breakout cables (QSFP+ to SFP+ DACBO, QSFP28 to QSFP+ DACBO). High-wattage optics (above 3.5 W) only in ports 32 to 63 on the AFI builds (guide, QFX5210-64C Port Panel Overview and Table 25)
features.optics-sfp-plus: 1 GbE or 10 GbE SFP+ transceivers (guide, QFX5210-64C Port Panel Overview)

performance.port-speeds: QSFP28 ports 0 to 63 run at 100 GbE by default and at 40 GbE with a QSFP+ transceiver. They run at 50, 25 or 10 GbE by channelization or breakout cable (up to 128 logical ports). The SFP+ ports run at 1 or 10 GbE

physical.weight-note: 23.44 lb (10.63 kg) without power supplies and fans, 31.09 lb (14.1 kg) with them (Table 26)

power.power-input-ac: 90 to 264 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 12 A at 100 VAC or 6 A at 240 VAC
power.power-input-dc: rated -48 to -60 VDC, operating range -40 to -72 VDC, 25 A maximum
power.redundancy-note: two supplies, 2N, each carrying the whole load; one may be removed at a time while the switch runs

thermal.fans: four fan modules and the fans in the two supplies; the switch runs 30 seconds without thermal shutdown while one fan module is replaced

ac-afi.description: QFX5210-64C-AFI: two 1100 W AC supplies (JPSU-1100W-AC-AFI) and four back-to-front fan modules (QFX5210-64C-FANAFI). All carry the label AIR IN and a Juniper Azure Blue handle (guide Tables 15 and 17).

ac-afo.description: QFX5210-64C-AFO: two 1100 W AC supplies (JPSU-1100W-AC-AFO) and four front-to-back fan modules (QFX5210-64C-FANAFO). All carry the label AIR OUT and a Juniper Gold handle (guide Tables 15 and 17).

chas.description: QFX5210-64C-CHAS, the chassis spare of guide Table 3: the switch with its two power supply bays and four fan module bays open, nothing seated.

dc-afi.description: Two 1100 W DC supplies (JPSU-1100W-DC-AFI) and four back-to-front fan modules (QFX5210-64C-FANAFI). The guide names these units but no chassis part number for the build.

dc-afo.description: Two 1100 W DC supplies (JPSU-1100W-DC-AFO) and four front-to-back fan modules (QFX5210-64C-FANAFO). The guide names the DC supplies (Table 3) but no chassis part number for the build. AC and DC supplies are never mixed in one chassis.

description: Juniper QFX5210-64C, a 2RU data-centre spine and leaf switch. It has 64 QSFP28 ports, numbered 0 to 63 in sixteen columns of four, and two SFP+ ports. The QSFP28 ports run at 100 GbE by default, at 40 GbE by transceiver, and at 50, 25 or 10 GbE by channelization. The port side also carries an RJ45 management port, an RJ45 console port, a USB port, a reset pinhole and four chassis lamps. The FRU side carries four fan modules, two power supplies and a two-hole protective earthing terminal. It ships as one front panel in several builds: AC or DC supplies, front-to-back (AIR OUT) or back-to-front (AIR IN).

gaps.wanted: The HPE datasheet a00150817enw, which the intake lists for a human to fetch. No datasheet figure is used.

Which lamps serve the inner ports of each column (1 to 31 odd, 32 to 62 even). The guide's Table 10 says four lamps for each QSFP28 port and its figures draw four lamps at the outer edges only, so the inner ports carry no lamp in the model.

The six round marks per column in the band between the two cages of a stack. The figures draw them as circles and the photograph shows ringed holes; the guide names them nowhere, so they are not drawn.
The two bi-colour lamps for each SFP+ port that Table 10 describes. No figure draws them and the photograph does not resolve any.
The bi-colour lamp the guide says is next to each fan module (Table 16). No figure or photograph shows where it is, so none is drawn.

The supply rating legend. Figure 8 prints 12-6A and 25A; the photograph of the real device prints 12-7A and 34A (Max); Tables 18 and 21 give 12 A at 100 VAC and 6 A at 240 VAC, and 25 A. The photograph's wording is drawn as printed; the tables' figures are in attrs.
Interface names are not printed on the metal and the guide's channelization text names none for this switch, so none are written.

The orderable part numbers of the DC and the AIR IN builds. The guide names the chassis spare QFX5210-64C-CHAS, the builds QFX5210-64C-AFI and QFX5210-64C-AFO (in its cautions), and the units but gives no SKU for the DC builds or any -S build, so the two DC builds are examples and not orderable.
An end-of-life announcement. None was searched for in this pass, and the guide states none, so the device states no lifecycle.

How many fan modules the switch can lose. The guide's Component Redundancy section says only that the switch has four fan modules and that a failed module that cannot keep the switch within its thresholds raises chassis alarms and can shut the switch down. Table 4 lists the fan modules as removable without action, and the cooling text says the switch runs 30 seconds without thermal shutdown while one is replaced. No N+1 form is claimed.
A power figure for a fan module. Table 3 and the cooling chapter give the airflow and the part numbers only; searched the cooling and power chapters and found whole-switch figures only.
The depth of the fan modules and of the supplies. The guide's figures are isometric and carry no scale and its tables state weights only.
The position of the front mounting brackets of the rack kit QFX5210-4PST-RMK. Figure 22 shows them in perspective with no scale; no position is written.

esd.description: the wrist-strap ESD terminal at the left edge of the port side (guide figure 12)

fans.description: QFX5210 hardware guide, Component Redundancy: four fan modules in the FRU panel, slots 0 to 3 left to right; all must be installed for optimal operation. The guide states no spare-fan form (N+1) for them.

grounding.description: the protective earthing terminal on the FRU side, two screws for a two-hole lug (guide figure 8 callout 2, Connecting the QFX5210 to Ground)

mgmt.mixed: the out-of-band panel at the right of the port side - an RJ45 management port, an RJ45 console port, a USB port and the recessed reset button. Four kinds, one purpose: reaching and recovering the switch when the data plane cannot.

attrs.redundancy-note: two supplies, 2N, each carrying the whole load; one may be removed at a time while the switch runs

qsfp28-leds.description: The four lamps above each column of QSFP28 ports 0 to 30 (even) and below each column of ports 33 to 63 (odd), only the first lit at 100 GbE and all four for a 10 or 25 GbE channelized port (guide Tables 10 and 11).

status-leds.description: The four chassis lamps ALM, SYS, MST and ID (guide Table 14).

name: qfx5210-64c

airflow-and-colour.note: Guide Tables 15 and 17: AIR OUT (front-to-back, port-to-FRU) units are Juniper Gold, AIR IN (back-to-front, FRU-to-port) units Juniper Azure Blue. The studio photograph of the AIR OUT build shows the fan handles and the supply handles orange, so orange is drawn for AIR OUT; no photograph of the AIR IN build is held and the blue is a plain azure. The guide's prose once swaps the two colours in a sentence about FRU-to-port fan handles; its tables and the photograph are used.

chassis.note: guide Table 26: 3.5 in (8.89 cm) high, 17.25 in (43.82 cm) wide, 22.83 in (57.99 cm) deep; 23.44 lb (10.63 kg) without power supplies and fans, 31.09 lb (14.1 kg) with them. 2RU (the guide says so, and 3.5 in is the 2U pitch of 88.9 mm). The inch figures are converted (88.9, 438.15 and 579.88 mm); the centimetre figures agree to the rounding. The width is the body between the ear folds: the guide says the front brackets of the rack kit make it 19 in, so the brackets are not modelled.

colour.note: The front plate samples about #939aa2 on bare patches of the studio photograph; the chassis colour is #949aa2, as the QFX5200 does. The photograph is lit warmly and these are its values, not a paint reference.

ears-and-kits.note: The guide describes mounting on four posts only, with a front mounting bracket on each side and a rear blade that slides into the rail, rails between 28 in and 36 in (71.1 to 91.4 cm) front to back in the mounting text and 23.6 to 36 in in the rack-requirements table. Table 3 and Table 36 name the kit QFX5210-4PST-RMK (front mounting brackets, rear mounting blades, twelve M4 flathead screws), shipped with the switch. The kit is NOT MODELLED and is not in `chassis.kits`, and no ear position is written: no figure measures where the bracket sits (figure 22 shows it in perspective).

esd-and-labels.note: The ESD point is the hex-nut-like jack at the left edge, 6.5 mm in and 38.5 down, with the ESD symbol beside it at 15.5 mm; the figure draws the same and the photograph shows a ring (a banana receptacle in a bezel). The photograph also shows a yellow pull tab at the right of the foot, 31 x 3.9 mm at 384.5 and 83.4 mm, which figure 10 draws as an outlined tab; it is drawn as a plain yellow plate and not as a label, since no text on it resolves. The guide draws no laser or hazard triangle and the photograph shows none.

gate-1.note: Figure 10 (a 1501 x 511 px raster of the port side, colour-coded by channelization block) is orthographic enough to measure across: its outline measures 1424 px between stroke centres (x 21 to 1445) against the table's 438.15 mm, 3.25 px/mm, and 285 px (y 30 to 315) against 88.9 mm, 3.21 px/mm. The aspect is 4.99 against 4.93, 1.3 percent out, so fractions are taken on both axes and the horizontal scale is used for x. Figure 8 (the FRU side, 1501 x 578 px) reads 1424 by 285 px as well. The studio photograph agrees on the repeating pitch (gang pitch 189 px at 4.14 px/mm is 45.7 mm against 45.45 from the figure), and its own body measures about 1811 px across, so it is read at 4.14 px/mm and checked against the figures. Figure 9 is the same side with callouts, 10 percent short in height, and was not measured.

logo-and-text.note: The maker's name and wordmark and the Junos OS mark are printed on the plate below the USB port, with the model text QFX5210-64C between them. The wordmark and the mark are logos and are NOT DRAWN, not even as text: two logo-zone regions hold their place (guide figure 10, photograph, 397 to 423 mm across). The model text is drawn.

mgmt-panel.note: Figure 11 and the enlargement of figure 12: at the right of the port side, an RJ45 management port (MGMT, em0, C0, 1000BASE-T) stacked over an RJ45 console port (CON) in one housing, a two-cage stacked SFP+ block (legends 0 and 1, see sfp-plus-numbering) and a USB 2.0 port beneath it. The housing is 17.8 mm wide (figure 58 px at 3.25 px/mm), the jacks are drawn as two std/rj45 jacks of 15.8 x 13.2 touching, so the pair is 26.4 mm tall against about 25 mm in the figure; the 1.4 mm excess is accepted. The management jack has its lamps at the top corners and its keyway at the top, the console jack the keyway at the foot, as the figure draws them. The jack positions are the figure's, 2.6 mm left of the photograph's. Table 13: the status lamp is green at 1000 M and amber at 100 M, the link/activity lamp green steady with a link and blinking with traffic. The USB port is USB 2.0 by the guide's callout, so it is drawn with the usb2 skin.

modules.note: The fan modules and the power supplies are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay: the supplies' own fans are inside the supplies, and the lamp the guide describes beside each fan slot (Table 16) is not drawn in any figure. Four fan modules (guide Table 3: QFX5210-FANAFI and QFX5210-FANAFO; Table 15 spells them QFX5210-64C-FANAFI and -FANAFO, the longer spelling is used) and two supplies (JPSU-1100W-AC-AFI and -AFO, JPSU-1100W-DC-AFI and -AFO, Table 3). They are the library's new components juniper/qfx5210-fan-afo, -afi and juniper/qfx5210-jpsu-1100w-ac-afo, -afi, -dc-afo, -dc-afi; the one existing supply with a similar rating, juniper/ex4300-jpsu-1100-ac-afo, is a different part number (JPSU-1100-AC-AFO, an EX4300 part) and is not reused.

port-lamps.note: Figure 9 and its enlargement draw four round lamps on a 4.1 mm pitch (44 px at 10.7 px/mm) centred on each cage column, above the top row (centres 4.4 mm above the cage's top edge, 14.2 mm down the face) and below the bottom row (4.4 mm below its foot, 78.1 mm), with the port numeral between the lamps and the cage on top and below the lamps at the foot. Table 10 says four bi-colour lamps for each QSFP28 port, only the first lit at 100 GbE and all four when the port is channelized to 10 or 25 GbE; Tables 11 and 12 give the colours (green steady for a link, green blinking for activity, amber blinking for beacon on the SFP+ lamps). THE FIGURES DRAW LAMPS ONLY AT THE OUTER EDGES OF THE FOUR-CAGE COLUMN, so the lamp groups are filed against ports 0 to 30 (even) and 33 to 63 (odd), the ones whose numerals they stand beside; the inner ports (1 to 31 odd, 32 to 62 even) have no lamps of their own in any figure, and the guide does not say which lamps serve them (see the gap). The band between the two cages of a stack carries six round marks per column, drawn in the figures as small circles; the photograph shows them as bright ringed holes in the cage bezel and not as lamps, so they are not modelled as lamps.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal and read off the photograph and the enlargements of figure 9: a numeral above the top cage of each column (the even ports 0 to 30), a numeral below the bottom cage (the odd ports 33 to 63), and between the two stacks a pair on one baseline, `N` and an up triangle at the left of the column centre for the odd port 2k+1 and a down triangle and `N` at the right for the even port 32+2k, so each triangle points at the cage its numeral names. Interface names are not printed and are not written (see the gap).

ports.note: Figure 10: 64 QSFP28 cages as sixteen columns, each column a stack of two cages above a stack of two (four cages), in eight gangs of two columns. A column holds ports 2k and 2k+1 in the upper stack and 32+2k and 33+2k in the lower stack (k = 0 to 15), as the printed numerals read. The colours of figure 10 are the guide's port blocks (channelization groups, Figure 10 "Block 0" to "Block 3") and not hardware. The cells are on the registry's qsfp-ganged pitch of 19.0 mm, the gangs are 45.6 mm apart (figure 45.45, photograph 45.7), so the gutter is 7.6 mm, and the first cage's left edge is 31.5 mm in (figure 31.1, photograph 32.4) and the last cage's right edge 388.2 mm (figure 387.7, photograph 387.8). The cage rows are 15.9 mm apart within a stack (figure 15.9) and the stacks 29.6 mm apart; the upper stack's top row is 18.6 mm down. THE FIGURE IS 1.3 PERCENT OUT IN ASPECT AND THE Y POSITIONS ARE FITTED TO THE TABLE'S HEIGHT, so they are estimated to about 0.5 mm.

power.note: Table 18 (AC): 357 W typical and 655 W maximum, input 90 to 264 VAC at 50 to 60 Hz, 12 A at 100 VAC and 6 A at 240 VAC. Table 21 (DC): 383 W typical and 696 W maximum, -48 to -60 VDC rated, -40 to -72 VDC range, 25 A maximum. Maximum is measured at 40 C with SR optics and 100 percent IMIX load, typical at 25 C with DACs and 50 percent load, excluding transceivers. The AC figures are filed as the device's.

rear-layout.note: Figure 8 (a 1501 x 578 px flat raster of the FRU side) and the studio photograph (2100 x 654 px, AIR OUT build, 4.1 px/mm across the body) agree to 1.5 mm: four fan slots on a 69.0 mm pitch from 85.0 mm (figure 84.3, photograph 85.7), the supplies 52.0 mm wide at 18.0 mm (slot 0, photograph 18.4, figure 17.5) and 368.0 mm (slot 1, photograph 367.7, figure 368.0), the supplies' tops at 45.2 mm and the fan tops at 23.5 mm. The earthing terminal is at 366.5 mm, 22.0 down. The photograph's vertical scale reads about 2 percent short of its horizontal one (the body is 87 mm tall on it at 4.10 px/mm, against 88.9), so heights are taken from the figure's 3.21 px/mm and checked on the photograph, where the supply's foot sits 1.7 mm above the figure's and the fan modules' 1.2 mm above; the supply is seated 0.8 mm higher than the figure puts it as a compromise between the two. Rear positions are estimated to about 1.5 mm.

rear-printing.note: DRAWING AND PHOTOGRAPH DISAGREE on the supply rating legend. The guide's figure 8 prints "AC INPUT : 100-240V ; 50-60HZ ; 12-6A Max" and "DC INPUT : -48V- -60V ; 25A Max"; the photograph of the real device prints "12-7A" and "34A Max", so THE PHOTOGRAPH WINS and is the legend drawn. Table 18 and Table 21 give 12 A at 100 VAC and 6 A at 240 VAC, and 25 A for DC; they are the figures in attrs, and the 7 A and 34 A of the metal are a conflict between the guide's tables and the printed legend, recorded as a gap. Also printed: the model plate QFX5210-64C at the left (the wordmark above it and the Junos OS mark beneath are logos, not drawn), a power symbol and the slot number (0, 1) beside each supply, a fan symbol and the slot number (0 to 3) at the top right corner of each fan slot (THE LEGEND IS DRAWN 5 TO 9 MM HIGHER, just above the slot, because the module paints the whole slot, bracket strip included, and would cover it), four small arrows along the top rim (at 150 mm and each 69 mm on) and the earth symbol beside the terminal. The photograph's five small ring screws above the fans and two beside the supplies, and the two corner thumbscrews, are not drawn.

sfp-plus-numbering.note: DRAWING AND PHOTOGRAPH DISAGREE. The guide's figures 9 to 11 print 64 above the SFP+ pair and 65 below it. The studio photograph of the real device prints 0 above and 1 below, so THE PHOTOGRAPH WINS: the legends are 0 and 1, and the two cages are `tengig-0` and `tengig-1` (the ids are named for the job and not the connector, which would collide with `port-0`). The guide's text calls them "two dedicated SFP+ ports" and, for interface numbering, 64 and 65 follow the 64 QSFP28 ports; that is kept here and not as a printed legend.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5210 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-03-09, 187 pages (copyright 2026 Juniper Networks), https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/qfx5210/qfx5210.pdf: the port panel figures 9 and 10 and the callout figures that enlarge them, the management panel figure 11 and the chassis status lamp figure 12, the FRU panel figure 8, the fan and supply figures 13, 16 to 19 and 21, the specification tables 3, 15, 17, 18, 21, 25 and 26, and the mounting chapter. Juniper's studio photographs of the 64C, port side and FRU side, 2100 x 700 and 2100 x 654 px (image library, qfx5210-64c-front-high and qfx5210-64c-rear-high). THE HPE DATASHEET (a00150817enw) IS NOT HELD (the intake lists it for a human to fetch), so no datasheet figure is used and the guide's tables stand in for it. No mechanical drawing, Visio stencil or 3D model is held for the QFX5210: the intake's MX stencil folder has none for it. A third-party elevation of the same box (a NetBox library PNG, held in the intake photo folder) was looked at to confirm what is on the FRU side and was not measured or copied. The guide and photographs are Juniper's and are used for reference; no drawing or photograph is copied into the library, every skin is drawn new from measurements.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4, as juniper/mx204 applies it): in each stack the upper cage is upright and the lower one turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between them. The photograph shows the bright lip of the lower cage of the upper stack on its upper edge and the upper cage's on its lower edge, which agrees, but at 4 px a cage it does not overturn the rule. The same for the two SFP+ cages.

status-lamps.note: Figure 12 and its enlargement: four chassis lamps ALM, SYS, MST and ID in a column at the left of the port side with their legends to the left, 3.5 mm apart on a pitch read at 10.7 px/mm and checked at 3.56 mm on the photograph, with the RESET pinhole above them and its legend beneath (figure 9 callout 1, 7). Table 14: ALM red for a major alarm and amber for a minor one, SYS green when Junos OS is loaded, MST green for a standalone switch (the guide's text says "three LEDs" once; it draws and names four), ID blue blinking for the beacon.

vents.note: Hexagonal perforations: a band along the top edge (1.6 to 11.6 mm down, 29.5 to 411.5 mm across), a half band along the foot (83.6 to 87.6 mm, 8 to 384 mm), a block at each side (2.5 to 10.5 mm and 430 to 436.5 mm across, 44 to 85 mm down), and a perforated strip in the gutter between every two gangs (7 strips, 4.6 mm wide). The guide's figure 10 draws the same fields as outlines. Drawn as vent strips on a 3.3 mm pitch; positions are read at 3.25 px/mm and 4.14 px/mm and are estimated.

bottom.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide's figures show no underside.

placements.description: Table 13 - the status lamp is green at 1000 Mbps and amber at 100 Mbps, unlit at 10 Mbps or link down; the link activity lamp is green steady with a link and blinking with traffic
Table 14 - red: major alarm, the switch halted; amber: minor alarm; unlit: no alarm or halted
Table 14 - green steady: Junos OS for QFX Series is loaded; unlit: powered off or halted
Table 14 - green steady: the switch is a standalone switch; unlit: offline or no power
Table 14 - blue blinking: the beacon feature is enabled (request chassis beacon); unlit: not enabled

left.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide's grounding and rack-mounting figures (22 to 25) show the side wall and the mounting rail in perspective only, with no scale from which a hole could be placed.

right.empty: Not drawn by any source held. No figure shows the right wall flat.

top.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide shows no figure of the lid except the serial number label location (figure 39), which is an isometric with no scale.
